title: Short-Term Rental (Airbnb) Law in Türkiye: 100-Day Rule & Permits
seoTitle: Short-Term Rental (Airbnb) Law in Türkiye 2026: 100-Day Rule
metaDescription: Understand airbnb law turkey 2026 under Law No. 7464: 100-day permit rules, unanimous building consent, 2026 fines, and investor ROI impact.
quickAnswer: Under airbnb law turkey 2026 — formally [Law No. 7464](https://mevzuat.gov.tr/anasayfa/MevzuatFihristDetayIframe?MevzuatNo=7464&MevzuatTertip=5&MevzuatTur=1) — renting any home for 100 consecutive days or fewer requires a Tourism Purpose Rental Permit from the [Ministry of Culture and Tourism](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/genel/bakanlikbelgelikonutlar.en.aspx). Apartment blocks require notarized unanimous owner consent, and unlicensed hosting carries 2026 fines starting at 180,617 TRY.

body.text: What does Türkiye's Tourism Purpose Rental Law require for stays under 100 days?

[Law No. 7464](https://mevzuat.gov.tr/anasayfa/MevzuatFihristDetayIframe?MevzuatNo=7464&MevzuatTertip=5&MevzuatTur=1) governs all residential leases of 100 consecutive days or fewer for tourism purposes. Before listing on Airbnb or Booking.com, owners must obtain a Tourism Purpose Rental Permit via [e-Devlet](https://www.turkiye.gov.tr/ktb-turizm-amacli-kiralanan-konut-izni-7918), mount the Ministry plaque at the door, and report every guest to police (KBS).

Tenants cannot sublet rented flats to tourists, and individual rooms inside owner-occupied homes are ineligible for permits. Contracts exceeding 100 days fall outside the permit regime, though signing more than four 101+ day contracts for the same unit in one year triggers an evasion penalty, per [2026 regulatory analyses](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/turkey/regulations).
Why is unanimous building-resident approval required in apartment blocks?

Law No. 7464 mandates notarized unanimous consent (oy birliği) from all condominium owners in multi-unit buildings to shield permanent residents from hotel-style turnover, noise, and security risks. In buildings exceeding three units, one host may hold permits for at most 25% of apartments, capping commercial consolidation inside residential blocks.
Because a single objecting or unreachable neighbor blocks approval, legal short-term hosting in ordinary Istanbul or Antalya apartment blocks is rarely viable. Two property types bypass this hurdle:

items: Detached Villas (Müstakil Konut): Standalone houses need no building-owner vote, though they still require a Ministry permit, plaque, and KBS guest reporting.
Serviced Residences (Yüksek Nitelikli Konut): Purpose-built residences with reception and security whose registered management plan (yönetim planı) explicitly authorizes short-term letting.

body.text: What penalties apply for unlicensed short-term rentals?

Unlicensed short-term hosting carries tiered administrative fines originally set at 100,000 TRY, 500,000 TRY, and 1,000,000 TRY in Law No. 7464 and revalued annually. In 2026, penalties start at [180,617 TRY on first detection](https://www.cbhukuk.com/en/airbnb-short-term-home-rental-fines-turkey/), rising to [903,088 TRY and 1,806,177 TRY](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/turkey/regulations) on repeat offenses, alongside 24-hour platform delisting orders.
How does this law change ROI calculations for investors?

Law No. 7464 ends the old "buy an ordinary city apartment and run it on Airbnb" investment strategy. Investors evaluating standard residential apartments in 2026 must underwrite returns on 12-month domestic leases — where [Istanbul net yields average roughly 4.1% to 5.0%](https://www.bosphorusbrokers.com/guides/rental-income-in-istanbul/) after expenses and Turkish income tax — rather than peak nightly rates.
If short-term tourism income drives your purchase, apply this investor checklist:

items: Target detached coastal villas or verified yüksek nitelikli konut serviced residences with explicit short-term clauses in their management plan.
Verify any seller's claim of an active license on the [Ministry of Culture and Tourism's public STR registry](https://www.ktb.gov.tr/genel/bakanlikbelgelikonutlar.en.aspx).
Budget for permit fees, plaque installation, KBS reporting, and Turkish rental income tax filings.
Stress-test ROI using 101+ day mid-term or 12-month long-term leases as a fallback.
Confirm Iskan and [TAPU title deed status](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/tapu-verification-turkey) before paying a deposit.

faq.q: What is the 100-day rule in Türkiye's short-term rental law?
faq.a: Under [Law No. 7464](https://mevzuat.gov.tr/anasayfa/MevzuatFihristDetayIframe?MevzuatNo=7464&MevzuatTertip=5&MevzuatTur=1), any residential stay of 100 consecutive days or fewer is a tourism-purpose rental requiring a Ministry of Culture and Tourism permit.

faq.q: Do detached villas in Türkiye need neighbor approval for an Airbnb permit?
faq.a: No. Standalone houses (müstakil konut) bypass apartment-block unanimous consent, though they still require a Ministry permit, plaque, and KBS guest reporting.

faq.q: What is the fine for running an unlicensed Airbnb in Türkiye in 2026?
faq.a: Revalued 2026 fines start around [180,617 TRY per property](https://www.airroi.com/airbnb-data/turkey/regulations) on first detection and escalate to 903,088 TRY and 1,806,177 TRY for continued violations.

faq.q: Can I bypass Law No. 7464 with 101-day contracts?
faq.a: Contracts over 100 days fall outside the permit regime, but signing more than four such contracts for the same home within one year triggers a heavy evasion fine.

faq.q: Can a tenant legally sublet a Turkish apartment on Airbnb?
faq.a: No. Law No. 7464 prohibits tenants from subletting residential units to tourists, imposing a per-contract fine for every unauthorized booking.
